conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have two children - Alex, who's 8, and Blake, who's 20. They both live at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have two children - Alex (8 years old) and Blake (20 years old), both living with you.

Let me ask about Blake first, since age is an important factor. Is Blake currently in approved education or training? (This could include things like A-levels, approved vocational training, or similar approved courses.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake isn't in any education or training at the moment. They finished their studies a while back.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Blake is 20 and not in approved education or training, they would fall outside the Child Benefit eligibility criteria (which normally covers children under 16, or under 20 if they're in approved education or training).

Now, regarding Alex who is 8 years old - I have a few questions:

1. Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

Does Alex work for 24 hours or more per week, or receive any benefits in their own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - they're only 8! And they don't receive any benefits in their own right either.

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, here's my assessment:

**For Alex (8 years old): ELIGIBLE ✓**
You would be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. Alex is under 16 years old, lives with you in the UK, doesn't work, and doesn't receive any benefits in their own right. This meets all the standard criteria for Child Benefit.

**For Blake (20 years old): INELIGIBLE ✗**
You would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Blake. Child Benefit normally covers children under 16, or those under 20 if they're in approved education or training. Since Blake is 20 and not currently in approved education or training, they fall outside the eligibility criteria.

**Overall:** You can claim Child Benefit for Alex, but not for Blake. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child, so if no one else is currently claiming for Alex, you should be able to make a claim.

Please note: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.
